surprises.head: Calgary brought the hits
surprises.body: Calgary’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 173, against their usual 101 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Matthews reaches 800 points, but the Maple Leafs lose
paras: Matvei Gridin and Mikael Backlund scored less than two minutes apart midway through the first to put the Flames up 2-0. Zack MacEwen and Jake Middleton squared off late in the period. Gridin scored again on the power play just 25 seconds into the second to make it 3-0 for the Flames. The Maple Leafs’ Kirill Marchenko left early in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Easton Cowan got the Leafs on the board midway through the period. William Nylander cut Calgary’s lead to 3-2 early in the third, with Auston Matthews picking up his 800th NHL point on the goal. Joel Farabee shut the door with an empty-netter with a minute and a half left, and Martin Pospíšil added an empty-net goal with 39 seconds left to make it 5-2. Gridin added an assist for a three-point night.

The Flames had the better of the chances, outshooting the Maple Leafs 34-28. Devin Cooley made 26 saves for the Flames, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 29 of 32 at the other end. The Flames moved to 5-6-0 and climbed to fifth in the Pacific, while the Maple Leafs fell to 7-5-2, third in the Atlantic.
